function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability**

| Aspect | What Turbonomic Brings | Why It Matters for Unilever |
|--------|-----------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Unified Visibility** | Aggregates real‑time telemetry from all workloads—VMs, containers, serverless functions, databases, etc.—across on‑prem, GCP, AWS, Azure, and other clouds into a single pane. | Unilever can see the entire application stack without switching dashboards or pulling logs from disparate sources. |
| **Intelligent Resource Allocation** | Uses machine learning to predict future demand, then automatically moves or scales workloads to the most cost‑effective, performance‑optimal resource pool. | Reduces over‑provisioning and under‑utilization, saving money while ensuring service levels for consumer‑facing apps. |
| **Policy‑Based Automation** | Lets you define business rules (e.g., “Keep latency < 200 ms for checkout services”) and Turbonomic enforces them across clouds. | Eliminates manual intervention and ensures compliance with SLAs across regions and vendors. |
| **Cost Optimization & Forecasting** | Provides real‑time cost attribution per workload, predicts future spend, and recommends rightsizing or spot‑instance usage. | Gives Unilever a clear view of where money is spent and how to cut waste—critical for a global FMCG company with tight margins. |
| **Performance & Reliability Assurance** | Continuously monitors CPU, memory, I/O, network, and custom metrics; alerts when thresholds are breached; auto‑remediates by moving workloads or scaling resources. | Keeps high‑traffic e‑commerce sites and supply‑chain analytics running smoothly during peak demand. |
| **Compliance & Governance** | Tracks regulatory requirements (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) and ensures data residency policies are enforced automatically. | Protects sensitive customer data across multiple jurisdictions. |

**Key Differences Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Observability Tools**

| Feature | Turbonomic | GCP Operations Suite (formerly Stackdriver) | AWS CloudWatch | Azure Monitor |
|---------|------------|-------------------------------------------|----------------|---------------|
| **Scope** | Cross‑cloud + hybrid (on‑prem + Kubernetes + SaaS) | Native to Google Cloud only | Native to AWS only | Native to Azure only |
| **Data Sources** | VMs, containers, serverless, databases, storage, networking, custom metrics | Cloud‑native services, logs, traces, metrics | Cloud‑native services, logs, traces, metrics | Cloud‑native services, logs, traces, metrics |
| **AI/ML Capabilities** | Predictive analytics for capacity, cost, and performance; automated remediation | Basic anomaly detection, alerting | Basic anomaly detection, alerting | Basic anomaly detection, alerting |
| **Automation** | Policy‑driven actions (move, scale, terminate) across clouds | Limited automation (Cloud Functions, Cloud Scheduler) | Limited automation (Lambda, EventBridge) | Limited automation (Logic Apps, Automation) |
| **Cost Attribution** | Detailed cost per workload, per business unit, per project | Cost breakdown by project, but less granular | Cost breakdown by service, but less granular | Cost breakdown by resource, but less granular |
| **Governance** | Unified policy engine that spans all clouds | Policies per GCP organization | Policies per AWS account | Policies per Azure subscription |
| **Integration** | Works with Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes, ServiceNow, PagerDuty, etc. | Integrates with GCP services only | Integrates with AWS services only | Integrates with Azure services only |
| **User Experience** | Single dashboard, unified API, role‑based access across clouds | Separate dashboards per GCP project | Separate dashboards per AWS account | Separate dashboards per Azure subscription |

### Bottom Line

Turbonomic acts as a *single control plane* that brings together the telemetry, cost, and performance data from all of Unilever’s environments—whether they’re on GCP, AWS, Azure, or on‑prem—and applies AI to make decisions that optimize for both cost and performance. Native tools give you deep insight into their own ecosystems but require separate dashboards, APIs, and governance models. Turbonomic unifies those silos, giving Unilever a holistic view and automated actions that span the entire multi‑cloud landscape.
